Why “gross margin” is not the right metric for a bank
- “Gross margin” (sales less cost of goods sold, divided by sales) is a manufacturing/retail concept tied to product cost. Banks do not report COGS; their businesses are interest‑ and fee‑based.  
- For banks, more appropriate profitability/efficiency metrics are: net interest margin (NIM), pre‑provision profit (or pre‑provision profit margin), efficiency/overhead ratio, return on assets (ROA), return on common equity (ROE), and provision‑adjusted measures. These capture the economics of lending, deposit funding, trading and fee businesses.

- 2020: 53,295 / 119,951 = 44.4%  
- 2021: 50,306 / 121,649 = 41.4%  (down 3.0 percentage points vs 2020)  
- 2022: 52,555 / 128,695 = 40.9%  (down 0.5 percentage points vs 2021)

2) Net income margin = Net income / Total net revenue
- 2020: 29,131 / 119,951 = 24.3%  
- 2021: 48,334 / 121,649 = 39.7%  (up 15.4 percentage points vs 2020)  
- 2022: 37,676 / 128,695 = 29.3%  (down 10.4 percentage points vs 2021)

Conclusion
- Because banks don’t use “gross margin,” it’s not the right indicator.
